prompt: Is it normal that I get nervous before every single presentation even after doing like fifty of them? Will it ever stop?
text:
Yes, this is very normal. Many experienced speakers, including actors, musicians, and professional presenters, still feel nervous before they go on. Fifty presentations is a lot of practice, but nerves don't come from lack of skill. They come from your body reacting to being watched and judged, and that reaction doesn't fully switch off.

**Will it ever stop?** For most people, it doesn't go away completely, but it usually gets weaker and easier to handle. Experience tends to change how the nerves feel more than whether they show up. After enough presentations, the racing heart and tight stomach stop feeling like a warning and start feeling like part of the routine.

**Some things that help:**

- **Reframe the feeling.** Nervousness and excitement feel almost the same in the body. Telling yourself "I'm fired up" works better than trying to calm down, because it doesn't fight your body.
- **Know your first minute cold.** The nerves usually peak at the start. If your opening is well rehearsed, you get through the worst part on autopilot.
- **Breathe slowly before you start.** Try a long exhale, about twice as long as your inhale. It lowers your heart rate.
- **Move a little.** Walk around, shake out your hands, or stand tall beforehand. It burns off some of the adrenaline.
- **Focus on the audience, not yourself.** Think about what they need from you rather than how you look.
- **Rehearse out loud.** Practicing in your head doesn't prepare you as well as speaking the words.

A bit of nervousness can even help. It keeps you alert and often makes you more engaging. It becomes a problem only if it gets in the way of your delivery or makes you dread presenting. If that happens, a public speaking group like Toastmasters or a few sessions with a coach can make a real difference.

Do the nerves hit you more before the talk or during the first few minutes? That can change which of these tips will help most.
